title: Shoulder Horizontal Adduction

checks.basis: horizontal adduction (AAOS norm 0-135 deg) carries the hand across the body: it should pass well beyond the midline (0.3+ shoulder widths). Reaching the other shoulder (0.5) flagged 23% of reps physiotherapists scored as good, so the midline-plus criterion is used
checks.label: Hand past midline (shoulder widths)

checks.basis: arm kept fairly straight: elbow within 40 deg of full extension
checks.label: Elbow angle

checks.basis: trunk side lean under 10 deg (trunk lean is the usual compensation for limited shoulder range)
checks.label: Lateral trunk lean

cues.ERR_NOT_ACROSS: Bring your arm further across your body, toward the other shoulder.
cues.ERR_TRUNK_LEAN: Keep your trunk upright; don't lean to the side.

source: Clinical thresholds (AAOS / Norkin & White norms, common compensation limits); false alarms measured on MobiPhysio videos physiotherapists scored >= 90 (Iqbal et al., Harvard Dataverse 2025, CC0)
